spec.description: Published videos, by video id, by broadcaster or by category. Exactly one of `id`, `user_id` and `game_id` is given; the remaining filters apply only alongside `user_id` or `game_id`.

request.title: GetVideosRequest
request.description: Which videos, and which page of them.

id.description: Video ids to get, such as `335921245`. Sent as repeated `id` query parameters; at most 100. Mutually exclusive with `user_id` and `game_id`.

user_id.description: The broadcaster whose videos to get. Mutually exclusive with `id` and `game_id`.

game_id.description: The category whose videos to get, at most 500 of them. Mutually exclusive with `id` and `user_id`.

language.description: Only videos broadcast in this language, as an ISO 639-1 two-letter code, or `other`. Only alongside `game_id`.

period.description: Only videos published within this period. Defaults to `all`. Only alongside `game_id` or `user_id`.

sort.description: The order to return videos in: newest first, biggest gains in viewership first, or most viewed first. Defaults to `time`. Only alongside `game_id` or `user_id`.

type.description: Only videos of this type. Defaults to `all`. Only alongside `game_id` or `user_id`.

first.description: Rows per page. Range [1, 100]; defaults to 20.

after.description: Cursor for the next page, taken from `pagination.cursor` of the previous response; omit for the first page.

before.description: Cursor for the previous page, taken from `pagination.cursor` of the previous response. The generated walk only pages forward, with `after`.

response.title: VideosFrame
response.description: The wire frame: one page of videos, and the cursor for the next.

id.description: An ID that identifies the video.

stream_id.description: The broadcast this video was recorded from; null unless the video is an `archive`.

user_id.description: The ID of the broadcaster that owns the video.

thumbnail_url.description: A URL to a thumbnail, with `%{width}` and `%{height}` placeholders to replace with the size you want. Twitch currently serves only 320 by 180.

view_count.description: How many times the video has been watched.

language.description: The language the video was broadcast in, as an ISO 639-1 two-letter code, or `other`.

type.description: The video's type: a past broadcast, a highlight cut from one, or a video the broadcaster uploaded.

duration.description: The video's length, written the way Twitch writes durations: `3m21s` is three minutes and twenty-one seconds.

items.title: MutedSegment
items.description: One stretch of the video Twitch Audio Recognition muted.

duration.description: How long the muted stretch lasts, in seconds.

offset.description: How far into the video the muted stretch begins, in seconds.

muted_segments.description: The stretches Twitch Audio Recognition muted; null where none were.

pagination.description: The cursor for the next page. Twitch sends this object empty once there are no more pages.

unverified.detail: No recording yet: Helix authenticates every call, and the machine this spec was written on holds no Twitch application credentials. The Record workflow fills this in: it reads the application client id and secret from the repository secrets TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET, mints an app access token through the core, replays this endpoint's `examples/*.request.json` with `truewire capture`, and opens a pull request with the response the API sent.

notes: The response schema is the wire frame, `{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`, and no `envelope.payload` is declared, so the method returns the frame and the rows are `result["data"]` (ADR 0010, authoring rule 6). Unwrapping `data` would put the pagination cursor out of reach: pagination paths resolve inside whatever the method returns, and Helix puts the cursor beside `data`, not inside it. One rule for every Helix method is worth more than unwrapping the five endpoints here that never page.

Twitch ends a walk by sending `pagination` as an *empty object*, not by omitting it and not with a null cursor, so the terminator is `absent_cursor` on `pagination.cursor` and a walk stops on the first page whose `pagination` holds no `cursor`.
`stream_id` and `muted_segments` are nullable on the wire, so both are `anyOf` with `{"type": "null"}` rather than a multi-type schema (authoring rule 5).

Written from the Helix reference at the `docs` URL above. Fields the reference marks deprecated are not declared; an undeclared field passes validation and is dropped from the validated value, so a recording that carries one is still valid. The first recording confirms or corrects the rest.
